_comment: The map. rows are row-major: rows[r] is board row r, and character i in that row is the hex at axial q = rowQStart(r) + i (see src/hex.js). Terrain ids must exist in data/terrain.json. Enemy placements, patrol routes, objectives and exfil are below.
name: Night Drop — first pass
_startHexes: Placeholder deployment, one per trooper in data/roster.json order. The drop phase at M6 replaces these with a chosen drop run plus seeded scatter. Spread across the three approach corridors of SPEC.md §8 so movement is worth testing.
_enemies: SPEC.md §6 and §8. A post has `at` and never moves; a patrol has `route`, starts on its first waypoint and walks the rest, `loop` true going round and false walking back. `type` is an id in data/enemies.json. `facing` is where it looks at the start, one of NW NE E SE SW W (pointy-top hexes have no straight north). The two track patrols are the two routes the hedgerow lanes cross (§8); the south-west post and its patrol are the patrol base the wood and ridge line passes.
_reserve: The reserve squad (SPEC.md §6). It enters once, on the first free entryHexes hex, the first enemy phase the alert is at Alarmed. The road leaves the map at the north edge, so that is where it comes in. It does not hunt: it marches to guardHex and stands there as a sentry facing guardFacing, toward the exfil. A man is out the moment he ends a move on exfil, so the guard watches the last stretch before it, not the exfil hexes themselves.
_objectives: SPEC.md §7. `kind` picks the numbers in data/rules.json objectives (charges needed, blast radius, alert, whether a scout can cut it, what its hexes become when destroyed). `hexes` is the footprint the art covers; `chargeHexes` are where a trooper stands to place a charge. Exactly one objective is `primary`. Charge hexes were chosen by simulating the patrols at Calm and Suspicious: the bridge's west-bank marsh is watched only when the bridge patrol passes, the exchange's north, east and south sides only when the village patrol comes round, and the dump's two ridge hexes differ (-1,6 is rarely seen, -1,7 often).
_exfil: SPEC.md §10. A trooper who ends a move on one of these is out. The south end of the canal towpath, also reachable from the hedgerow lanes, away from all three drop runs.
